neighbours.label: a verb of reach or spread over a range, just before its scope complement (extends to/beyond, spread to, traced or reaches back to)
fire: The mountain range extends from the coast to the central plateau.
Voting rights were later extended to women over thirty.
The custom can be traced back to the Roman occupation.
Her authority extends well beyond the walls of the school.
The rumour spread to every village in the valley within a day.
The drought has extended into a third year.
Their friendship reaches back to their days at primary school.
The company's network now extends across four continents.
quiet: The mountain road leads to a quiet lake near the plateau.
Voting cards were later mailed to women over thirty.
The custom was described in a book about the Roman occupation.
Her office is just behind the walls of the school.
The rumour was repeated by every villager in the valley.
The drought ended in its third year.
Their friendship began at primary school.
The company now sells in four continents.

notes: Card: extends/extended/extend, 'traced back', Chinese 遍/延长; the pole promotes ' to', ' beyond', ' into', ' across'. Probes: extends to 0.67, extended beyond 0.73, traced/reaches back 0.62-0.81, spread to 0.41-0.51; leads to 0.14, applies to 0.14, extended family 0.14, refers to 0.08.
